Bean, Broad / Bean, French / Bean, Runner / PeaBirdsTorn podsrecognisePigeons eat seeds and young leaves; sparrows tear pea pods. Birds may pull young beans or damage runner-bean flowers.actProtect the crop as soon as damage appears.preventUse securely supported netting or wire guards; keep it taut, clear of plants and check for trapped wildlife.

Bean, Broad / Bean, French / Bean, RunnerBlack Bean AphidAphids on leavesrecogniseDense black colonies on soft broad-bean tips can stunt growth and distort flowers and pods. French beans may be affected in midsummer.actPinch off infested broad-bean tips; squash small colonies where needed. PeaPea AphidAphids on leavesrecogniseLarge aphid colonies can check pea growth and damage flowers, although small numbers rarely cause serious trouble.actMonitor first; squash damaging colonies by hand and let natural predators help.preventEncourage aphid predators and keep checking tender growth. Bean, Broad / Bean, French / Bean, Runner / PeaPea and Bean WeevilNotched leavesrecogniseU-shaped notches appear along young leaf edges. Grey-brown adults drop when disturbed. PeaPea ThripsSilvery podsrecogniseTiny dark or yellowish insects cause silver patches and small holes on leaves and pods. Hot, dry weather favours damaging attacks.actCheck for insects; water stressed plants, encourage predators and tolerate minor damage.preventKeep plants watered and growing steadily; clear the crop after harvest.

Bean, French / Bean, RunnerNo PodsrecogniseRunner-bean flowers fall without pods after drought or hot weather; cool weather may reduce pollination. French beans can also drop flowers when dry.actWater roots thoroughly during dry spells, especially from flowering. PeaPea MothMaggoty peasrecognisePale caterpillars feed inside pods, leaving damaged peas and frass. Flowering crops are vulnerable during summer egg laying.actOnce caterpillars enter pods there is no useful treatment. Discard affected peas when shelling.preventUse early or late sowings to avoid peak moth activity, or cover with insect-proof mesh before flowering.

PeaMarsh SpotBrown-centred peasrecogniseA brown-lined cavity inside peas, sometimes with slight yellowing between leaf veins, indicates possible manganese shortage.actExisting damaged peas cannot be repaired. Bean, BroadChocolate SpotSpots on leavesrecogniseChocolate-brown spots on broad-bean leaves can merge; stems, flowers and pods may also be affected. Cool, damp, crowded crops are most at risk.actRemove badly diseased plants and clear infected remains after cropping.preventImprove spacing and airflow. Do not save infected seed; consider spring sowing if autumn crops repeatedly suffer.

Bean, French / Bean, RunnerHalo BlightSpots on leavesrecogniseWater-soaked leaf spots with yellow halos and wet-looking pod lesions may indicate bacterial halo blight.actRemove and destroy diseased plants.preventUse healthy bought seed. Remove diseased debris, rotate crops and avoid handling wet foliage.

Bean, French / Bean, RunnerAnthracnoseDry spots on podsrecogniseSunken dark pod spots, stem cankers and brown leaf patches may develop pinkish margins on French and runner beans.actRemove badly diseased plants. PeaDowny MildewMouldy leavesrecogniseYellow patches above pea leaves correspond to mauve or brown mould below. Cool, wet weather favours infection; pods may distort.actRemove affected leaves and severely diseased plants.preventRotate crops, reduce crowding and avoid prolonged leaf wetness. Water early if foliage will get wet.

PeaPowdery MildewrecogniseWhite powdery patches affect leaves and sometimes pods, often on late crops. Bean, French / PeaGrey Mould (Botrytis)Rotten podsrecogniseSoftly rotting pods or stems develop fuzzy grey mould, especially in wet weather and crowded crops.actRemove mouldy pods and damaged material promptly.preventKeep picking, avoid crowding and improve airflow; minimise prolonged wet foliage.

Recently cultivated grassland is more exposed.actIdentify the grubs before acting; similar soil larvae are not always harmful.preventRemove confirmed damaging grubs found during cultivation. All listed cropsRoot RotRoot troublesrecogniseDark, decaying roots accompany wilt. Gummy lesions may also affect stems; fruit can develop black rot.actRemove badly affected plants and debris. All listed cropsSun ScaldPapery patchesrecognisePale brown, papery patches develop at leaf margins after excessive sun; dry tissue shrinks.actScorched tissue will not recover.preventProvide greenhouse shading and ventilation while keeping roots evenly moist.

All listed cropsAnthracnose (Leaf Spot)Spots on leavesrecognisePale leaf spots enlarge and turn brown with yellow margins. They may merge; stem lesions can develop pink growth, then darken.actRemove affected leaves and badly diseased plants.preventUse clean containers and fresh compost; ventilate and avoid splashing foliage.

All listed cropsSclerotinia RotrecogniseDark rotten fruit develops white cottony mould containing conspicuous black resting bodies.actRemove infected fruit promptly and dispose of diseased material.preventKeep fruit clear of soil and avoid water splashing onto it.

All listed cropsVerticillium WiltYellowing leavesrecogniseLower leaves yellow, then dry and wilt; brown streaks inside stems are a clue, not a diagnosis alone.actConfirm the cause and remove badly affected plants. Maintain even moisture without waterlogging.preventUse clean containers and fresh compost isolated from affected ground; clear infected debris.

Onions and ShallotsSet DivisionrecogniseOnion sets may form twin bulbs; large sets and growth checks can contribute. Shallots naturally form clusters.preventUse suitable onion sets, plant in season and maintain steady growth. Shallot division is normal.

Onions and ShallotsBirds Pulling SetsNewly planted onion sets are pulled out of the soil just as they begin to grow.recogniseNewly planted onion sets are pulled out before they establish. Onions and ShallotsOnion FlyTunnelled bulbs with 1/4 in. white maggots.recogniseYellow, drooping leaves accompany maggots feeding at bulb bases. Excess nitrogen or deep sowing may contribute.actUse sound affected bulbs early; do not store them with well-ripened bulbs.preventAvoid overfeeding and deep sowing.
